This item needs adaptation to an asked sketch task while retaining q1; all three distractor explanations also need specific mistakes: option 1 subtracts g, option 2 changes the constant -1 to +1, and option 3 negates the quadratic term.

quiz.q2: Selecting a combined equation is not an asked booklet type; adapt this item to an asked sketch task while retaining q2. Replace the generic distractor explanations: option 0 subtracts g, option 1 changes -2 to +2, and option 2 uses -(x^2+2) for f before adding g.

quiz.q3: Selecting a combined equation is not an asked booklet type; adapt this item to an asked sketch task while retaining q3. Replace the generic distractor explanations: option 0 adds the linear term and makes both constants positive, option 1 negates the quadratic term while retaining the difference constant, and option 3 adds g instead of subtracting it.

quiz.q4: Standalone identification of this vertical asymptote is not asked in the source; adapt q4 to a source sketch task. The generic distractor explanations do not name mistakes: option 0 confuses the oblique and vertical asymptotes, option 2 uses the reciprocal component's horizontal asymptote, and option 3 mistakes the numerator for the excluded input; explicitly distinguish domain and asymptote in the solution.

quiz.q5: Standalone identification of this vertical asymptote is not asked in the source; adapt q5 to a source sketch task. Replace the generic distractor explanations: option 1 uses the reciprocal component's horizontal asymptote, option 2 mistakes the numerator for the excluded input, and option 3 confuses the oblique and vertical asymptotes; explicitly distinguish domain and asymptote in the solution.

quiz.q6: Standalone vertex finding is not asked in this source section; adapt q6 to an asked difference sketch. Replace the generic distractor explanations: option 0 selects the positive x-intercept, option 1 adds 6 instead of subtracting it, and option 2 selects the negative x-intercept.

quiz.q7: Standalone symmetry classification is not asked in this section and is not central to this target skill; replace q7 with an adapted source sketch task. The generic distractor explanations also fail to identify the mistakes: option 0 overlooks h(-x)=h(x), option 1 confuses y-axis symmetry with reflection in y=x, and option 3 confuses even and odd symmetry.

quiz.q8: Standalone symmetry classification is not asked in this section and is not central to this target skill; replace q8 with an adapted source sketch task while preserving mastery:true.
